AgentForge

One Idea. Six AI Agents. One Complete Blueprint.
Fully observable with OpenTelemetry → SigNoz.

Architecture · Database · Backend · Frontend · Testing · Observability


AgentForge is a multi-agent AI pipeline that takes a one-line product idea and generates a complete software blueprint — requirements, architecture, database schema, backend API surface, frontend structure, and testing strategy — in a single streamed build.

Powered by Groq (llama-3.3-70b-versatile) and instrumented end-to-end with OpenTelemetry → SigNoz.


--- ## Why AgentForge? ### Your AI agents shouldn't be a black box. Multi-agent AI systems are powerful, but once several agents begin chaining LLM calls and making decisions, understanding what happens inside the pipeline becomes difficult. When a build becomes slow, expensive, or fails, developers need answers: - **Which agent is slow?** - **Why did this build fail?** - **How many tokens did each agent consume?** - **How much did the build actually cost?** - **Which LLM calls were unnecessary?** - **How much did caching and deterministic rules save?** AgentForge makes those answers visible. Every build is instrumented with **OpenTelemetry → SigNoz**, exposing traces, metrics, structured logs, token usage, cost, latency, cache/rule decisions, dashboards, and alerts across the AI pipeline. > **AgentForge doesn't just build with AI — it shows you exactly what the AI is doing.** --- ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Client UI["Workspace UI"] end subgraph Backend SSE["SSE"] Orch["Orchestrator"] Agents["6 AI Agents"] Resolve["Cache → Rule → LLM"] Groq["Groq Service"] end subgraph Observability OTel["OTel Collector"] SigNoz["SigNoz"] end UI --> SSE SSE --> Orch Orch --> Agents Agents --> Resolve Resolve -->|Hit| Orch Resolve -->|Miss| Groq Backend -. Traces .-> OTel Client -. Traces .-> OTel OTel --> SigNoz ``` ## Build Sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as Browser participant S as SSE Route participant O as Orchestrator participant A as Agents (x6) participant G as Groq API participant C as OTel Collector participant D as SigNoz U->>S: GET /api/build/stream (EventSource) S->>O: start build activate O loop per agent O->>A: run agent A->>A: check cache (hash of title+desc+prompt) alt cache hit A-->>O: cached result (0 tokens, 0 cost) else check rule template A->>A: try deterministic rule template alt rule match A-->>O: templated result (0 tokens, 0 cost) else A->>G: chat completion G-->>A: content + token usage A-->>O: result + real cost + metrics end end O-->>U: SSE "agent" event (source: cache | rule | llm) end O-->>U: SSE "finished" event deactivate O par telemetry (continuous) U->>C: frontend spans (page load, sse_stream) O->>C: backend spans, metrics, logs C->>D: ingest end ``` --- ## Cost & token savings — cache and rule-based resolution Every agent call resolves in this order before it ever reaches Groq: 1. **In-memory cache** — keyed on a SHA-256 hash of `agentName + title + description + previousOutputs + systemPrompt`. An identical request served twice returns instantly, at zero token cost. 2. **Rule-based templates** — deterministic, hand-written templates for common patterns that don't need an LLM call at all. 3. **LLM (Groq)** — only reached on a genuine cache/rule miss. Every agent result carries a `source: "cache" | "rule" | "llm"` tag, shown live in the UI as each agent completes. ![Agent results with rule badges](./images-readme/rule.png) ![Agent results with llm badges](./images-readme/llm.png) ![Agent results with cache badges](./images-readme/cache.png) This isn't just a UX nicety — it's measured. On a cache or rule hit, the tokens, cost, and latency that call *would* have spent are recorded as savings, not just skipped: | Metric | What it tracks | |---|---| | `agentforge.generation.tokens_saved` | Tokens avoided by serving from cache | | `agentforge.generation.cost_saved_usd` | USD avoided by serving from cache | | `agentforge.generation.latency_saved_ms` | Milliseconds avoided by serving from cache | | `agentforge.generation.failures_avoided` | Potential LLM failures sidestepped by a cache hit | | `agentforge.generation.cache_hit` / `cache_miss` | Cache effectiveness, per agent | | `agentforge.generation.rule_hit` | Requests resolved by template instead of cache or LLM | | `agentforge.generation.llm_call` | Requests that actually reached Groq | All of these are labeled by `agent`, so you can see exactly which agent benefits most from caching in the dashboard. --- ## What's instrumented | Signal | Where | Examples | |---|---|---| | **Traces** | Client + Server | `build.sse_stream` (frontend), `AI Build Pipeline` → per-agent → `Groq API Call` (backend) | | **Metrics** | Server | `agentforge.build.{count,failed,duration,cost,cost_microusd}`, `agentforge.agent.{duration,cost,cost_microusd,tokens}`, `agentforge.generation.{tokens_saved,cost_saved_usd,latency_saved_ms,failures_avoided,cache_hit,cache_miss,rule_hit,llm_call}` | | **Logs** | Server | Structured build lifecycle logs, correlated to `trace_id`, including cache/rule hit events | | **Alerts** | SigNoz | High failed-build rate (>3/5min), agent p95 latency (>10s) | | **Dashboards** | SigNoz | Build throughput, latency, cost by agent, success/failure split, failure reasons | Cost is tracked per-agent and per-build, computed from Groq's real token usage (`prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens`) against a rate card in [`server/src/config/pricing.ts`](server/src/config/pricing.ts) — update that file if Groq's pricing changes. Frontend and backend currently emit **separate** traces (not yet linked by a shared `traceparent`, since native `EventSource` doesn't support custom request headers) — a natural next step if you want a single unified trace spanning browser → server.

--- ## Project Structure ``` AgentForge/ ├── client/ # React + Vite frontend │ └── src/ │ ├── telemetry.ts # OTel Web SDK setup │ └── services/ # SSE stream client ├── server/ # Express backend │ └── src/ │ ├── agents/ # 6 pipeline agents + cache/rule/LLM resolution │ ├── cache/ # In-memory generation cache │ ├── orchestrator/ # Build orchestration (stream + non-stream) │ ├── observability/ # Metrics + trace helpers │ ├── config/pricing.ts │ └── telemetry.ts # OTel Node SDK setup ├── pours/deployment/ # SigNoz docker-compose stack ├── dashboards/ # Exported SigNoz dashboard JSON └── alerts/ # Exported SigNoz alert rule JSON ``` --- ## Setup & Run Locally ### Prerequisites - Node.js 18+ - Docker + Docker Compose - A [Groq API key](https://console.groq.com) ### 1. Start SigNoz (observability stack) ```bash cd pours/deployment docker compose up -d ``` Wait ~30-60s for all containers to report healthy, then open **http://localhost:8080** and create your account. Collector endpoints exposed: `:4317` (gRPC) and `:4318` (HTTP). ### 2. Start the backend ```bash cd server npm install ``` Create `server/.env`: ```env PORT=5000 GROQ_API_KEY=your_groq_api_key OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318/v1/logs ``` ```bash npm run dev ``` Runs on **http://localhost:5000**, exporting traces/metrics/logs to the collector automatically on start. ### 3. Start the frontend ```bash cd client npm install ``` Create `client/.env`: ```env VITE_SIGNOZ_URL=http://localhost:8080 VITE_SIGNOZ_DASHBOARD_ID= VITE_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318/v1/traces ``` ```bash npm run dev ``` Runs on **http://localhost:5173**. > The collector's CORS config (`pours/deployment/ingester/ingester.yaml`) must > allow `http://localhost:5173` for browser-sent traces to reach it — already > configured in this repo. ### 4. Import dashboards & alerts In the SigNoz UI: - **Dashboards → New Dashboard → Import JSON** → [`dashboards/agentforge-dashboard.json`](dashboards/agentforge-dashboard.json) - **Alerts → New Alert** → follow the step-by-step guide in [`alerts/agentforge-alerts.md`](alerts/agentforge-alerts.md) to recreate both alert rules (this SigNoz build creates alerts through the UI wizard rather than raw import; `alerts/agentforge-alerts.json` documents the underlying query shape for reference) ### 5. Build something Open **http://localhost:5173**, describe a product idea, hit build — watch the 6 agents stream in, then check SigNoz Traces/Metrics for the full pipeline. ![Build Analytics](./images-readme/build-analytics.png)
